note: The Kingdom of Galicia, created as a separate realm for García II when Ferdinand I of León-Castile divided his domains (1065), was rapidly reabsorbed into León after García's deposition by his brothers Alfonso VI and Sancho II (1071). The Galician territorial identity persisted, however — its separate legal customs, its pilgrimage route to Santiago de Compostela, and the Galician-Portuguese dialect that eventually became Portuguese. The County of Portugal, carved from Galicia in 1093 and granted to Henry of Burgundy, eventually broke away to become an independent kingdom (1139).

_quarry.structural_significance: Galicia's brief independence and subsequent reabsorption into León demonstrates how dynastic division and reabsorption shaped Iberian political geography; the more lasting legacy was Portuguese independence — carved from Galician territory — which created a distinct Atlantic-facing Iberian state
